mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best defines a consistent system of two linear equations in two variables?

options.A: A system that has exactly one solution.
options.B: A system that has no solution.
options.C: A system that has infinitely many solutions.
options.D: A system that has at least one solution (either a unique solution or infinitely many solutions).

mcqs.answer: A system that has at least one solution (either a unique solution or infinitely many solutions).
mcqs.explanation: A consistent system is one that possesses at least one solution. It may have a single (unique) solution or infinitely many solutions. Options A and C describe only part of the possibilities, while B describes an inconsistent system.

mcqs.question: The pair of equations 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 12 is:
mcqs.explanation: The second equation is not a multiple of the first because 4x + 6y = 10 would be the exact double. Since the left‑hand sides are proportional but the constants are not, the lines are parallel and never intersect, giving no solution.

mcqs.question: How many solutions does the system 3x - 2y = 7 and x + y = 2 have?
mcqs.explanation: Solving the second equation gives x = 2 - y. Substituting in the first yields 3(2 - y) - 2y = 7 → 6 - 5y = 7 → y = -0.2 and x = 2.2. A single ordered pair satisfies both equations, so the system has a unique solution.

mcqs.question: Consider the pair of equations 5x - 3y = 2 and 10x - 6y = 4. How many solutions does this system have?
mcqs.explanation: The second equation is exactly twice the first (both sides multiplied by 2). Hence both equations represent the same straight line, leading to infinitely many points of intersection.

mcqs.question: Which statement is true about the system x - 2y = 3 and 2x - 4y = 10?
mcqs.explanation: Both equations have the same left‑hand side ratio (the second is twice the first), but the constants are not in the same ratio (3×2 = 6 ≠ 10). Therefore the lines are parallel and distinct, giving no point of intersection.

mcqs.learning_point: Use coefficient relationships to classify a pair
mcqs.question: For the system a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, which condition guarantees that the system is inconsistent?
mcqs.explanation: When the ratios of the coefficients of x and y are equal but differ from the ratio of the constants, the two lines are parallel with different intercepts, leading to no intersection (inconsistent). Option B gives infinitely many solutions, C indicates intersecting lines (consistent), and D is insufficient.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the type of system with its description?

options.A: Consistent – No solution; Inconsistent – Exactly one solution
options.B: Consistent – At least one solution; Inconsistent – No solution
options.C: Consistent – Infinitely many solutions only; Inconsistent – Unique solution only
options.D: Consistent – Unique solution only; Inconsistent – Infinitely many solutions only

mcqs.answer: Consistent – At least one solution; Inconsistent – No solution
mcqs.explanation: A consistent system is defined as one that possesses at least one solution (either a single point or a whole line of points). An inconsistent system has no solution. Options A, C, and D invert or restrict these definitions.

mcqs.question: For what value(s) of k does the system 3x + 4y = 7 and 6x + 8y = k become inconsistent?

options.D: No value of k makes the system inconsistent

mcqs.explanation: The second equation is twice the first on the left side. If k were also twice 7 (i.e., 14), the two equations would represent the same line (infinitely many solutions). Any other value of k makes the constants not proportional, giving parallel distinct lines and thus no solution (inconsistent).
